junction.name: St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street, New York City

claims.text: St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street had 81 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 22 pedestrians injured, 26 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.5 million a year.
30% of crashes here involved a two-wheeler, against 16% at the city's priority junctions.
17% of crashes here had a cyclist hurt, against 7% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead and a two-wheeler was involved in 29% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 14% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.4 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $832,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.3 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $433,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for St Nicholas Avenue, West 125 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10
Subject: Request for safety study at St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

For the 5 years from 31 October 2021, the official record shows 150 crashes at St Nicholas Avenue & West 125 Street, including 81 injury crashes. 22 pedestrians and 26 cyclists were injured, and no one was killed. This is a City priority location. The yearly cost of the harm is $5.5 million in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars). A Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2024 is the latest recorded safety project.

Please carry out a safety study at this junction and, on the roads you are responsible for (St Nicholas Avenue and West 125 Street), consider:

- longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals), which is expected to prevent about 4.4 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,509,000 in harm per year and paying for itself if it costs less than $10.6 million to install. Please first check on site for an entry on yellow or red.
- reflective backplates on the traffic signals (Backplates with Retroreflective Borders), which is expected to prevent about 2.4 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $832,000 in harm per year and paying for itself if it costs less than $5.8 million to install. Please first check on site for an entry on yellow or red.

Thank you for your consideration.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
